You told Mr. Manning that you didn't have any knowledge of the fact that that was done. Can you tell the Trial Chamber whether you have any knowledge, based on your familiarity with these events, why the letter O would have been erased and replaced with a T for some of these MPs who you saw at the Orahovac school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I wasn't privy to those things, who would write or erase anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, sir. I have no further redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Judge Mindua has a question for the witness. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Not madam but Mr. Judge Mindua. Sir, I would like to ask you to clarify something, and I'm thinking about the 65 ter summary that the Prosecutor read out to us on page 6 and 7 of this morning's transcript. So if the transcript is right, the commander of the military police was Jasikovac; is that right? Miomir Jasikovac; is that right? He was the commander of your company, of your military police company? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were in the Opel Rekord car and you had the keys of the car, and with him you followed the trucks in which the prisoners had been placed and you followed them until the spring water, and you did it three or four times, and every time the vehicles carried on and you went back, but why did you go back and why didn't you follow the trucks all the way?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I was told that I should do, that I should reach the water fountain and then return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you were with Commander Jasikovac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was next to the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you were alone, then, in the vehicle? There was no officer with you in the car? Is that what I should understand?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was on my own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what was your role, then? Were you just driving or were you supervising the movement of the vehicles? Because I don't really understand what you were supposed to do, then.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was told that I should follow the trucks until we reached the water point, and that I would then have to return, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fair enough. So I'd like to ask you a last question. So you never saw these alleged executions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, you will be pleased to hear that this is the end of your examination in this trial. The Chamber would like to thank you that you came here to The Hague and were able to provide us with your answers and your knowledge. Now you are free to return to your normal activities. Thank you again. And the Court usher will assist you while leaving the courtroom. Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, is the next witness ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The next witness is ready, Mr. President. We did have a question we wanted to clarify and it's pursuant to Honourable Judge Mindua's last question. What we saw -- what we see in the transcript as translated into English was: "So you never saw these alleged executions; is that right?" And we just want to make sure that that indeed was the question as opposed to: "So you never assisted these alleged executions?" So we just want to be clear for the purposes of the record that the correct question was -- or that the question was translated correctly and that the witness understood the correct question. So if we could just have some clarification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's very clear in the English interpretation, we heard what is recorded. "So you never saw these alleged executions?" That was what I heard in interpretation in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The issue, Mr. President, is whether that's what the question was originally asked by the Honourable Judge Mindua in the first place in French, was it "saw" or "assisted?" I'm being told that some French-speaking folks who were listening in heard the question as "assisted" these executions and not "saw" these executions. So I just want to make sure that we've got the question correctly put to the -- put to the witness in his own language after it's been translated from French and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think Judge Mindua is in a position to clarify what was the content of his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course I can be of assistance. I just wanted to find out if the witness had indeed seen these alleged executions. I never said that -- I never asked him whether he assisted in these executions, absolutely not. And I think that it was correctly translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Gajic, now what about the B/C/S translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the most important thing is what is it that the witness heard and what sort of question he answered. The question as interpreted to the witness was whether the witness was present when the executions were taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Yes, it is exactly what I said. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think now we have it clear on the record, the mutual understanding in all languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, it's a -- I think we all understand but I just want to -- we may want to call the witness back because seeing executions is different from being present at the executions. One can see the execution but not be present, so just to -- just so we have absolute clarity, it may be worth bringing the witness back and just clarifying that, just to make sure that he is hearing it exactly as how Honourable Judge Mindua asked it to the witness, because it is different from -- it sounds to me like a different question once it's been translated, whether you saw something versus whether you were present at an execution, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I see another reason to call the witness back, there were in fact two questions in one and he said no. And if it is referring to the first part of the question, then it's different than to the second part. We should call the witness again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, first, please -- witness, please sit down. I have to explain you are called again because one part of your testimony was unclear due to a problem with interpretation to different languages, and we would like to clarify one thing. I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth still applies for this short, last part of your examination. Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Since Mr. Thayer is the party who called the witness, and in view of the fact that it was Judge Mindua who put the question to begin with, I think it is only up to the Trial Chamber to put that question again now, rather than either of the parties. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perfectly right, Mr. Tolimir. That was the intention of the Chamber. Judge Mindua will repeat his question and put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We had a problem with the English translation. We didn't receive interpretation, and Judge Mindua is so kind to repeat the question again. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I shall repeat the question, Your Honour. Witness, you said that you followed with your Opel Rekord the trucks and you did that three or four times and you followed the trucks where the prisoners had been placed, and every time you stopped at the water spring, and I asked you a question, I wanted to know whether you had seen the presumed or alleged executions. Did you have the opportunity to see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Since the trucks proceeded on their way for perhaps up to 300 metres, then there is an overfly, and one needs to proceed up that slope, so no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To be complete, did you hear any shootings at these occasions?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not at that point, no. I would reach the water spring by car, I would make a U-turn there, and go back in the direction of the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you didn't wait for the return of the truck?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think now it is clear for the Chamber and the parties what the position of the witness is. Thank you very much again, and now I have to say again you are free to return to your normal activities. All the best for you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the next witness should be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vanderpuye. As it is the first time this year we have you in the courtroom, all the best for the upcoming months.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Only 11 left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Mr. President, I just wanted to raise as a preliminary matter that I would be requesting a caution pursuant to Rule 90(E), I think it is, as concerns the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First of all, good morning, sir, welcome to the courtroom. Please read aloud the affirmation on the card which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I solemnly declare that I shall speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down and make yourself comfortable. Before Mr. Vanderpuye is commencing his examination-in-chief, on his request I would like to give you a caution. Rule 90(E) of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, I would like to read out for you. I quote: "A witness may object to making any statements which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent Prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." Did you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Vanderpuye is examining you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, again, Mr. President, good afternoon to you, Your Honours and everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Ristic. As you know my name is Kweku Vanderpuye. On behalf of the Prosecution, I will put some questions to you regarding your evidence today. And before we get started, I just wanted to remind you to try to keep your voice up, speak a little bit more slowly than you would normally so that will give the interpreters an opportunity to translate what you're saying accurately to the Trial Chamber. And if there is anything that I ask you that is unclear to you, please let me know, and I'll try to rephrase it in a way that we can better understand one another. Let me begin as follows: Do you recall testifying in the case of Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al on the 16th, 17th, and 18th of April 2007?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to review the entirety of that testimony before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you listen to an audio recording of that testimony?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Ristic, having listened to your testimony, can you confirm that it accurately and fairly reflects what you would say were you to be examined here today and I were to put to you the questions, the same questions, as were put to you in that testimony?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Everything was correct, everything that I said, and I could now repeat everything again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will offer into evidence the witness's prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is 65 ter 06751. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I understand it's been assigned P1233 pursuant to a memo from the Registrar of 20 October 2010.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have it in front of me, but it will be received with this number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would also like to tender the associated exhibits that were admitted through there witness in the prior proceeding, as well as the exhibits that were used with him and tendered through other witnesses. They are P1234 -- oh, I see. P1234 through P1242.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: These are the category B exhibits, am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The category B exhibits are 1234 through 1240, and then I think 1241 and 1242 are category C exhibits. These are just documents that were used with the witness but tendered through other -- through other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you going to use them today with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't intend to use them with the witness, Mr. President, but they are being offered because in this particular circumstance, the witness was shown during the -- during his prior testimony certain tactical intercepts, and there is a commentary in there, there is some questioning back and forth on those intercepts during the course of his testimony, so I think they are inextricably interwoven and it would be beneficial to the Trial Chamber to have those exhibits before it in order to assess accurately the testimony, the nature of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Pursuant to the procedure this Chamber is following, you know that there must be some showing of relation between the prior testimony and these documents, not admitted through this witness in the previous trial. You may use them or not. It's up to you. Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will receive the documents P1234 through P1240.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have a -- I think a relatively brief summary I'd like to read into the record. In 1995, the witness served as the deputy commander of the Zvornik Brigade's 4th Infantry Battalion under Battalion Commander Pero Vidakovic. On the 1st of July in the absence of Commander Vidakovic the witness took charge of the battalion. That day, he attended a meeting at which the Zvornik Brigade commander, Vinko Pandurevic, informed all the battalion commands of the upcoming operation concerning Srebrenica. The witness was ordered to send a reconnaissance platoon to Konjevic Polje on 4 July 1995. The witness remained in charge of the 4th Battalion as deputy commander until Vidakovic's return on 18 July 1995. On the 6th of July, the brigade command notified the battalion that the Srebrenica operation had begun. It was similarly notified that the VRS had taken over the enclave on the 11th of July 1995. On the morning of 14 July 1995, the witness sent an Intervention Platoon to the area of Snagovo which was threatened by the advancing Muslim column pursuant to the orders of Zvornik Brigade deputy commander Dragan Obrenovic. That afternoon, a soldier from the battalion approached the witness saying that he had heard that a large group of people had gathered near the school in Orahovac. The soldier, who was from Orahovac, asked the witness what was going on there as he wanted to leave his position to return to defend the village. Concerned that this soldier, like many others in the battalion from Orahovac, might abandon the lines, the witness said he would check into what was going on. The witness radioed the brigade and the brigade's duty service to inquire what was going on, and he was told: "Do your work, this is no business of yours." He then phoned a friend in Orahovac who confirmed that a group of prisoners had indeed been brought to the school. Later that afternoon, the witness received a radio call from the brigade's deputy chief of security, Milorad Trbic. Trbic requested that the witness send around 10 men to help secure the prisoners claiming that they were trying to break out. The witness complied. Sometime later, one of the soldiers he had earlier dispatched to the school contacted the witness. The soldier reported that his unit was being forced to carry out executions. The witness told him that the men should not do anything and that he would come to the school immediately. When the witness arrived, he saw several soldiers in front of the gym. The witness saw Trbic, who was leaving the area, along with two lawyers in the Zvornik Brigade military police; Cedo Jovic and Goran Bogdanovic. In the school yard, the 4th Battalion soldiers approached the witness. They asked the witness to allow them to go home. The witness testified that "most likely he looked for Drago Nikolic," Drago Nikolic was the brigade's assistant commander for security and chief of security. However, the witness did not see him. Nevertheless the witness did see the commander of the brigade's military police company, Miomir Jasikovac and other military police officers whom he knew, including Nada Stojanovic, a female MP whom he saw bringing water toward the gym. He did not, however, speak to anyone concerning the situation or the executions about which his men had called him. At their request, the witness allowed his men to leave and ordered their return to the battalion command the following morning at 0800 hours. Whilst looking for his driver, as he was himself preparing to leave, the witness walked in the direction where he had seen Stojanovic, from the side of the school building he was able to see into the gym where he saw the prisoners. He also saw a tarpaulin covered TAM truck backed up to a door near the side of the gym. The witness stated he "could have supposed what was going on" but he did not investigate or inquire. He simply headed back to the battalion, passing several soldiers positioned near a water point off the main road. In all, the witness was at the school for about ten minutes. When he arrived at the battalion command, the witness called a meeting of the command staff to organise the battalion's defence. The Zvornik Brigade duty officer, Dragan Jokic, later informed the witness that a large group of Muslims was moving from Snagovo toward the 4th Battalion command from the rear. At around 0430 hours on the 15th of July, the battalion was attacked by the ABiH 2nd Corps from the front. Later that morning, it was also shelled. Major Obrenovic, together with Captain Milan Jolovic, aka Legenda, arrived at the command at around 1330 hours. Late that afternoon, the witness spoke to Zvornik Brigade Commander Pandurevic who assured him that his battalion would receive assistance. The attack lasted until around mid-day of 16 July when the battalion command post was ultimately abandoned. Many casualties were incurred before a corridor was finally opened allowing the Muslim column to pass through the defence lines. During his testimony, the witness denied ever speaking to Major Obrenovic in code about the events in Orahovac. He denied Obrenovic's assertion that Drago Nikolic had intervened as the witness -- as the witness sought to withdraw his men from the school that afternoon. The witness claimed that a member of his battalion, Gojko Simic, who was identified by a survivor as an executioner at Orahovac, was not on duty with the 4th Battalion at the time as he had been granted leave to attend his son's send-off to the army. The witness confirmed that no investigation or disciplinary action concerning the involvement of 4th Battalion soldiers in the events that occurred in Orahovac on 14 July 1995 was ever conducted or meted out respectively. Mr. President, that concludes my summary. I do have a few additional questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Ristic, before you became the deputy commander of the 4th Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade, did you hold any other position in that -- in the battalion? Did I misspeak? I misspoke. No, I didn't misspeak.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I used to be the assistant commander of the battalion for intelligence work, and that during the period of two years, from March 1993 to March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was your position -- did your position also involve, in addition to intelligence work, security work?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just so we are clear, can you tell us what your title was?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Assistant commander for intelligence and security work.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated that you did it for about two years; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And during the course of carrying out that work, did you work with members of the security organ of the -- at the brigade level?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in particular, who did you work with?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: With the Chief of Staff of the brigade, with the commander of the military police, with members of the military police. It all depended on what was necessary. It depended on what kind of help we needed from them in carrying out our tasks, if we had encountered problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were assistant commander for security and intelligence in the 4th Battalion, did you work with Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was Drago Nikolic's position at the time?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: He was the chief of security in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During your prior testimony, you also mentioned Milorad Trbic. Did you work with him as well during the period of time that you were assistant commander for security and intelligence in the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. At the end of that period of my work, I can't remember whether Trbic arrived then or later. We didn't co-operate much because his function was the assistant commander of a certain battalion. Now, when exactly he came to work with Drago Nikolic, I don't know, but we did not co-operate much. We spent more time co-operating with the commander of the military police, and the military police, in relation to arresting and detaining soldiers who were trying to avoid going to the front line. And also if there were other problems, such as quarrels or brawls or similar stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In July 1995, during the period of time -- well, rather I should say, when you saw him in Orahovac, did you know what Milorad Trbic's position was?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just so that we are clear for the record, can you tell the Trial Chamber what his position was at that time?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: As far as I knew, he was an assistant to the chief of security of the Zvornik Brigade, or maybe he was his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You mentioned that you worked also with members of the military police during the period of time that you were assistant commander for security and intelligence in the battalion. In particular, can you tell us who you worked with within the military police?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Our job was as follows: If any problems were discovered within companies, such as soldiers who did not show up at the defence line, they would report this by calling us through the phone line that went all the way up to the line. So they would report those people to us in the battalion. I, as the assistant commander for security, would then write out an order for the military police to bring them back, or sometimes in agreement with the commander of the company, we would call those people up by the phone to check why they didn't show up. And then it would be up to us to decide whether the police should be sent out to bring the people back to the line in order to work in the shift that had been assigned to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I just want to clarify a couple of things before I go back to my question. You said that you would be notified when, for example, a soldier didn't show up for duty. And would you be notified by somebody in the respective company of their absence or where did that notification otherwise come from?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: That notification came from the company commander or if he was absent from the platoon commander. If there was neither the company commander nor his deputy. So they would be the ones to tell us about those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You indicated that you would, as assistant commander for security and intelligence, you would issue an order for the military police to bring that person back. Can you tell us a little bit about that? What did that entail specifically?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, it meant that it was only them who could bring those people. My job could have also been done by the commander of the battalion. Indeed, if we were out there doing some other things, such an order could have simply been issued through radio links. It would simply entail the names of the people, and then the military police, acting on an order received from their own commander, would go out, find those people, and bring them into the brigade. We would then take over those people, unless they would send them directly where they had to be. It all depended on the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You mentioned that the military police would act on the orders of their own commander in order to bring these people in. Let me ask you: Was it incumbent upon you, as the assistant commander for security and intelligence at the battalion level, to notify the military police with respect to an individual that -- an absentee soldier or somebody that just didn't come into work, so to speak, at the company they were assigned?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to other types of issues that might arise with respect -- concerning, I should say, soldiers, you mentioned quarrels and things of that nature, was the procedure that you followed essentially the same in terms of notifying the military police to take action with respect to certain conduct which had been reported to you?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: When there were quarrels between soldiers, then we would resolve it, us in the battalion, commander, members of the command, and the security organ, we would try to find out what was going on, and we would try to settle the situation. If we were unable to do that, we would go and seek the help from the military police, military police attached to the brigade, the security organ of the brigade, and sometimes even the brigade commander, if it was a bigger issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In the circumstances where you were providing with information or came into information as assistant commander for security and intelligence, that a soldier had engaged in, let's say more than inappropriate behaviour but criminal behaviour, theft, assault, things of that nature, was it incumbent upon you to report that to your commander first? And was it incumbent upon you to report that to the military police or to the security organ at the brigade level?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you reported matters involving criminal behaviour at the -- I should say to the military police, were the military police obliged to act on the report that you gave them?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, they would act in line with our report. So if the soldier in question was a member of our battalion in the Zvornik Brigade, they would act accordingly. They, in the brigade, also had a legal department which could help -- which could help them. We on our level were not competent to resolve such cases because it was a state of war and it was them who had the appropriate arms, side arms, to do that. So as I said they had a legal department, they were higher command, higher than us in the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But it was incumbent upon you in your position to act on that -- on information, for example, that a soldier had committed a crime, is that -- is that fair?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that we filed those reports. It would be an invitation for an interview, and they would hold those interviews in the legal department or at the security organ in the brigade and then they would file the report. It wasn't us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that but I mean, you've indicated that if you received information, you would, or were required - and you correct me if I'm wrong - to report that to the military police so that they could go and arrest somebody because you, that is your office, assistant commander for security and intelligence, didn't have the authority to go and arrest people. Does that sound right?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: We did not have the authority to arrest. We would file a complaint in case something would happen with -- between soldiers or on the line itself or in the vicinity of the command. Anything else that happened elsewhere, for instance in a cafe or in the village where they lived or on a road, we could -- couldn't handle that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we are clear on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I see we've reached the break, Mr. President. This is as good a place as any to pause, and I'll move to another hopefully very brief area when we come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we break, I would like to clarify one thing with the witness. You told us that you had been the assistant commander of the battalion for intelligence and security work for the period from March 1993 to March 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What was your duty or your post after that period? That means after March 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was the deputy commander of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We must have our second break now and we will resume at 1.00, and the Court Usher will assist you during the break. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Ristic. Just a couple of questions briefly. As the assistant commander for security and intelligence at the battalion level, would it be fair to say that one of your responsibilities was to certainly report crimes that were reported to you, either to superiors within the security administration at the brigade level, to your own commander, to the military police?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was our duty to report events of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that the military police, at least in terms of the Zvornik Brigade, that you didn't have a military police battalion -- company, I should say, in your battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was the military police organised at the brigade level?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had the military police company and the commander of the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not there was a similar organisation at a more-superior level, the level of the corps, for example? Did the military police also exist at the corps level? In your case, it would be the Drina Corps, since the Zvornik Brigade was a part of that corps, but do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that, because I was never at the corps. So I don't know but I assume that probably they did have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I want to show you some photographs. First I'd like to show you P663. Let me show you, then, P0 -- P61, P00061. All right. We have it now up on the screen. Mr. Ristic, can you tell us what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: It is the gym which was part of the Orahovac school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like you to do is I'd like you to mark it because I'll ask you some questions concerning some of your observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ristic, can you identify for us where it was that you first arrived in the school yard? And if you could, indicate that by putting a number 1 on the photograph in the location that you are able to identify.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: When I entered the school yard, I went approximately to the centre of that yard, and then my men approached me. Should I put the number 1 there?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You indicated that your men approached you and where were they when you first saw them? And if you could indicate that with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I didn't see where they were. They probably saw me and then approached me, but I assume that they were around the gym where they were posted as sentry and close to the gym and the entrance to the gym, because they arrived there at about the same time that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If you're not able to mark it, that's all right. We have what you've said on the record. You indicated in your testimony that you saw Commander Jasikovac, commander of the military police company of the brigade. Can you indicate on this photograph, then, with the number 2, where you saw commander Jasikovac?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you could, could you indicate with the number 3 where you saw military police officer Nada Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, it was in the same area where Jasikovac was. It was there by the fence of the school, of the courtyard. They were both standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You indicated in your testimony that you saw a TAM truck near the gym. Could you indicate where that was or where you saw it by placing a number 4 on that location?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also indicated in your testimony that you saw Milorad Trbic, Cedo Jovic, and Goran Bogdanovic. If you're able to see where you observed them on the 14th of July 1995, could you mark that with the number 5, if they are in different places, obviously, 5, 6 and 7, if that may be appropriate, and if you can't determine it from this photograph, we'll see if we can look at another one.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I think I need another photograph because they were opposite the school building, and not -- they were not facing this school yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to tender this photograph, please, as marked, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This marked photograph will be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P1755. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness, please, P1384.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photo is not good either.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I want to ask you just a couple of questions about this photograph in any event, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First of all, do you recognise what's depicted in it?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, we see the gym here too. The Orahovac school gym. And the playground in front of the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to see on this photograph the area in which you were able to look into the gym on -- that you've indicated in your testimony? And if you are, if you could mark that with a number 1, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that the same general area that you were able to see military police officer Nada Stojanovic carrying some water?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same area where she was carrying the water. And as I passed, I walked alongside her and I saw that she was taking the water to the prisoners who were held at the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you could, it would be helpful if you could indicate with an arrow the direction that you were walking.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this exhibit as marked as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P1756, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness 65 ter 1131, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Takes a long time today but it is coming up.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think we have it on the screen now. Are you able to recognise what's depicted in this photograph, Mr. Ristic?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's the gym at the school that you were -- at -- in Orahovac where you were on the 14th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, judging by what I can see in this photo, it could be any gym. I'm not so familiar with the interior of the gym because I had never gone in, so I can't really claim that this was the Orahovac gym, but it would seem, judging by the photo, that this is the gym. In the photo we saw a little earlier you could see the gym more clearly, the particular gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And per this photograph as you see it, can you indicate which side of this building you would have been on on the outside of it?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, there is a door at the opposite end of this basketball board. It's on the school side.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And if you could just -- if you can't see it in the photograph, mark the photograph with an arrow pointing in the direction of this -- of this door.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this -- does this fairly approximate the state of the gym as you recall it when you were -- when you went to the Orahovac school gym on the 14th of July 1995? Does it look like the gym that you saw?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it seems to be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you were looking inside the gym, were there any other military personnel in and around the entrance to the gym where you were or otherwise inside the gym where the prisoners were?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, there weren't any soldiers inside. They were around the gym. They were there, posted by someone who was there, so they were the guards of the people who were inside. They were -- the soldiers were around the building in order to guard the prisoners who were inside the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to tender this photograph as marked as well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P1757. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness P1383.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph, Mr. Ristic?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to approximate from this photograph where you saw Milorad Trbic, Cedo Jovic, and Goran Bogdanovic?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Some 50 metres beyond this point where the school is, that's where the truck was that they were entering.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you could indicate with an arrow in the direction that you saw the vehicle and Trbic, Bogdanovic, and Jovic? And you've indicated it was about 50, 5-0 metres down this road; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some 50 metres from the edge of this photo, this part of the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I think that's pretty clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to tend they are photograph as marked as well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received too.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours this document shall be assigned Exhibit P1758. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: As long as we have this on the screen, just for a little bit of perspective, if you're able to estimate about how far it is from the school, that is, from the right side of the photograph, over to the far side of the gym? Can you approximate how many metres that might be? And if not, that's all right as well.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately some 30 metres or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Ristic. I'd like to show you one last photograph and that is P1644. Do you recognise what you see in front of you, Mr. Ristic?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to have you mark this photograph as well with the help of the usher, please. Can you see on this photograph the road that you took to go to the school and leave the school on 14 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Should I mark the road?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could indicate on the particular road that you took, number 1, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if you're able to, can you indicate with an arrow the direction in which the school is from the point that you've indicated -- that you've marked on the road?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In the direction that you've indicated, that is to the right of number 1 in the photograph, can you tell us about how far the school is from this point?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, probably some 250 to 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you indicate with the number 2 the area near the road where you said during your testimony that you saw some soldiers near a water point? Or a water source?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Tell us approximately how many soldiers you saw in the area that you've marked number 2 in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: There were a couple of soldiers there, two or three, in the area that I could see, so there were two or three soldiers there, and around this water point, that's where they were. Behind it, there was a road which was forking off to the right from where I was, but there were also some other soldiers behind that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you able to see that on this photograph? And if not, could you put an arrow in the direction that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: They were in the same area, in the direction where I was headed, towards the school. So from this water point towards the school, there were some soldiers. I don't know if they were walking in the direction of the school or just standing there, but I will put an arrow there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photo will fix what the witness has said, so could we just have the arrow placed at the point where the road -- where the point on the road actually was? Because he's just indicating the direction but not the actual spot where they were. So could we have the photo -- another photo a bit moved to the right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, this is the frame of the photo. We can't move it, and you may find another photo during your cross-examination to ask the witness to mark it. Here, the witness just draw an arrow in the direction. Mr. Vanderpuye? You should be aware of the time you used.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm acutely aware of it. I just have a couple of other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, can you indicate with the number 3 where the water source or water point is that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Next is are you aware that an exhumation was carried out in Orahovac with respect to the executions that occurred there on 14 July 1995? Were you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I found out later.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know approximately where that exhumation was carried out relative to the photograph that you have in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, because when IFOR arrived and when they found that pit, I could see from the direction of Kitovnice that place and their transporters; however, I don't know the exact location. It must have been somewhere around the railway track. I only saw it from afar but I never came closer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the railway track that you're referring to, is that the track or at least -- is that depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Just for the record, is that the -- is that the track that appears in the bottom half or path that appears in the bottom half of this photograph, straight line from left to right or right to left?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Ristic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I appreciate your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you tendering --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to tender this last exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P1759, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And just for the record, you have used a little more than one hour instead of 30 minutes, just to be clear on that. Mr. Tolimir, you may commence your cross-examination now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to greet the witness and wish him a successful stay here as well as return to his home, to Republika Srpska. I would like to thank him because he came here to testify on the relevant events.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So while the photo is still on the screen, I would like to ask the witness something about it, if it's all right with you. First, for the record, let us state that this is P1759. The Prosecutor requested from the witness to mark on this photo both the places that he saw at the relevant time and the places that were relevant after the war when SFOR came to this location. So first I want to ask you: How much time elapsed between the events themselves and the arrival of the SFOR soldiers who arrived there to secure the general area of the grave? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I cannot be precise about that but it must have been several months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just for the record, at the moment we have P1644 on the screen. The other one, P1759, is the marked photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. So now we don't see the markings that the witness put on the previous photo. That's good. Now we have a new photo. My words pertained to the state of the previous photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's up to you, Mr. Tolimir. Do you want to have the marked photograph back on the screen or do you prefer this photo without markings?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't want this photo. I want the other photo, the photo with the markings made by the witness as a response to the question by Mr. Vanderpuye about where exactly SFOR was located.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's in the process of uploading into e-court. If you want to give us another five minutes, it will be ready for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That will be P1759. In the meantime, you should put additional questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That is why I emphasised for the record that the markings were made on 1759, and that he was requested to mark both the locations that he saw afterwards, after several months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To have it clear on the record, the markings are in the photograph P1759, but they were made on the original photo like we see it on the screen now, that was P1644. The photograph -- it's the same photograph, one with markings, one without markings. Please continue your examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If it's uploaded, you may have that one with the markings on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. My question is as follows.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you see this photo that contains your markings, markings that pertain to the relevant period, the time when the events were going on?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you required today to enter into this very same photo the markings pertaining to the events that occurred several months later, when SFOR arrived to Bosnia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, they asked me whether I knew the place. I said I didn't know, but this photo shows the road that I took and that was -- the road used by several soldiers, and it also shows the water fountain right next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what exactly is marked by the arrow pointing towards the west?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: That's the direction of the school. There were several soldiers there, they were standing or walking on that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry I had to interrupt you. You are using the same language and you are overlapping again. Please be careful. The interpreters have to catch what you are saying. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise on my behalf and on behalf of the witness. I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did you see anything in the vicinity of this arrow, in this very spot where the arrow is?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: No, nothing except a few soldiers. I cannot remember whether they were standing still or walking on this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were they slightly below this arrow or were they exactly where the arrow is?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I didn't mark their exact position. It is the direction. They were somewhere in between this point and the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. How many metres would it be from this -- from the edge of the photo towards the school?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: If we look from the water fountain, number 3, there must be between 10 and 20 metres between that point and the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I think that the record is not clear as to what exactly you saw there. Thank you. When exhibit number P1131, according to 65 ter numeration, was shown to you, page 72, line 19, the Prosecutor asked you whether that was the school in Orahovac where you were on the 14th, and in line 19 you said that you were not inside the hall but that it looks like the gym, the hall, that you saw. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: It looks like a gym/hall but it could be also some other gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm asking you because you marked an arrow on that photo. So that arrow pertains to what you assume to be or to what you actually saw?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: The arrow shows the door. I approached the door in order to look inside, to look inside the gym. The arrow itself shows the door on this side of the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. That arrow, does it mark the direction where the door is because we cannot see the door itself in the photo?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: Just the direction of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: For the record, were you inside the gym shown to you by the Prosecutor, the gym visible on this photo, the gym in the school in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I did not enter the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I ask you this because I received interpretation of the Prosecutor's question which went along the lines, can you recognise it, but you cannot recognise something that you haven't seen.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR RISTIC
utterances.text: I didn't recognise it because from the inside it could have been any gym, and I never entered this particular gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I would like to interrupt you for a moment. There is one thing I have to clarify. On page 81, lines 8 and 9, I am quite confused. Witness, in the previous photo, the aerial image, you have drawn an arrow to the right-hand side of the photograph, and you were indicating or one answer was recorded as following: I quote line 8 and 9: "If we look from the water fountain, number 3, there must be between 10 and 20 metres between that point and the school." Do you stand by that, 10 to 20 metres from this water point, or was it a different distance to the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the water fountain, to these people, that's 10 to 20 metres. The school itself is 2, 300 metres, maybe even more than 300 metres away. So I was speaking only about the people that I saw there, standing or maybe walking towards the school or away from the school. I can't really remember now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You mean the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That clarifies the situation. We have now reached the time for the break for today. Mr. Tolimir, you may continue your cross-examination tomorrow. And, sir, we have to break now and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom. Please be reminded that it is not allowed to have any contact about the content of your testimony to either party. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
